data.title: Smoke Test
data.tagline: A smoke test uses a few critical checks after a new build to decide whether the system is worth deeper testing.
data.learningOutcome: You can select a few probes whose failure should block later checks.
data.description: A new version can open home, log in, and call a core API first; any failure blocks slower tests. It aims to decide “continue or stop” within minutes. Re-running every old feature and edge case is regression testing, not smoke testing.

learning.assumes: You know a new version can fail at basic startup or login.
learning.outcome: You can select a few probes whose failure should block later checks.

distinctions.label: Regression test
distinctions.explanation: A Smoke Test uses a few key paths to decide quickly whether a new build is worth deeper testing. A Regression Test more broadly checks that a change did not break existing behavior.

explanation.title: Decide whether deeper work is worthwhile
explanation.text: If home cannot open or login wholly fails, dozens of detailed cases mostly create noise. Smoke tests select the few basic, critical capabilities that expose an obviously unusable version early.

explanation.title: A failure needs a blocking action
explanation.text: Record the version and symptom, then fix or replace the test-environment version. Passing smoke does not mean enough quality; it only means deeper testing is worthwhile.

data.boundary: Smoke testing is neither full regression nor merely checking that a service started. It checks a few critical abilities to decide continue or block, not to prove every old feature remains intact.

lessonPractice.title: After a new build deploys, the home page will not open. What should the team do next?

options.label: Record the version and failure, block the full regression run, fix it, then restart from smoke tests
options.feedback: Correct. A failed key probe means this version is not worth deeper test investment yet.

options.label: Run every payment, filtering, and settings case first, then revisit the home page
options.feedback: The basic entry is already broken, so many later results are hard to interpret and waste time.

options.label: Declare that every historical feature has regressed
options.feedback: One failed home page cannot establish that every old feature failed; block and locate the current version first.

data.agentPrompt: After every deployment to the test environment, run smoke tests: home opens, login works, and the core API responds. If any fails, stop later regression, record the version and evidence; continue only when all three pass.
